$comment: Hand-labelled evaluation set. See WRITEUP.md for the labelling rubric and README.md for how to run the eval.

rubric.sampling: 20 reviews chosen by stratum, not at random: 2 spam, 2 junk, 3 non-English, 2 members of duplicate clusters, 4 multi-issue, 3 where the star rating contradicts the text, 4 ordinary. Random sampling of 20 out of 300 would have been ~95% ordinary English single-issue reviews and would have measured nothing interesting.
rubric.severity: Anchored to consequence for the user, not tone. Blocked out / money moved / data lost = critical.
rubric.categories: Every issue in the review, as a set. Order does not matter. Spam and junk carry no categories.

labels.note: Work-from-home scam with a shortened link. No product feedback at all.
Crypto airdrop spam.
Forum-style 'First!!!!' post. Not spam - just contentless.
Judgement call: a thumbs-up carries a weak positive signal but nothing actionable, so it is excluded from the issue report. Sentiment still labelled positive - the eval scores that separately.
German: app crashes constantly since the last update. Carries a 4-star rating, which contradicts the text.
Chinese: works well and looks good, but too expensive. Rated 1 star, which contradicts the text.
Spanish: charged twice this month, wants a refund. Money moved wrongly, so critical.
Canonical member of a three-channel cross-post cluster.
Clean twin of a 'Regret payign' typo variant - only fuzzy matching catches this pair.
Two distinct issues. Crashes on every launch is high, not critical - no data loss stated.
Billed after cancelling drives severity to critical. Rated 5 stars, contradicting the text.
Slow support plus a price rise. Annoying, but nothing is broken or blocked.
An earbud complaint filed against a meal-kit product - the source data mismatches product and text. Labelled on what the text says, not what the product is.
Genuine praise and a genuine complaint, so mixed rather than negative.
Negative tone but the only concrete issue is a feature wish, so severity is low. Rated 5 stars.
Near-identical issue to the row above but positive framing - a good test of sentiment vs severity independence.
Completely locked out - the user cannot use the product at all.
Praise for support does not lower the severity of being locked out by a 2FA loop.
Friction, not breakage.
Contains the word 'free' but is a legitimate complaint - the case a naive spam regex gets wrong.

$comment2: expectedDuplicateClusters and expectedNotDuplicates were built by reading every pair in the corpus scoring above 0.60 trigram similarity within a product (43 pairs) and judging each by hand. Labelling rule: a cross-post is the SAME review text re-posted to another channel, so only typos and punctuation may differ. The negatives are the near-misses that share a template opener or a complaint clause but are separate pieces of feedback - the highest scores 0.806, which is why the threshold sits at 0.88.
